backend.scope: single-node loopback object store in one OOM-protected container; not a cloud, multi-node, fleet, media or power-loss claim

fixture.subset: the frozen augmentation subset: the 272 MB embedding + 100 name-sorted evenly spaced tensors = 101 tensors, 424,439,296 logical bytes

durability_contract.native_arms: a completed write is every object PUT acknowledged by the provider
durability_contract.weftfs_arms: every blob PUT acknowledged by the provider, then one commit record accepted that names them; all-or-nothing for a reader
durability_contract.note: the pipeline reports durability_model=provider-ack on S3 and issues no file barrier; the MinIO data directory is a tmpfs
durability_contract.visibility: single-node read-after-write and list-after-write for published keys; conditional PUT (If-None-Match/If-Match) required and probed at open

arms.interleaving: rotated by one position per repetition, as the augmentation contract requires

adverse.proxy: bench/scripts/s3_fault_proxy.py (byte-level forwarder, one fault per run)

losses_and_non_claims: the provider-ack durability model is not a media or power-loss guarantee
one host, one loopback object-store process, one writer
the fault proxy is test infrastructure and cannot reproduce a real provider's partial-failure modes
no claim about AWS S3, GCS, Azure or any cloud service
pipelined rows are labelled ablations: the pipeline is a store API (Store::prepare_tensor_group_pipelined), not a shipped CLI verb
